Secondly, when they entered the village, the civilians go towards Djakovica; that is to say, that they come to the road where our blockade was. They are going from the village towards Djakovica. They are now going to the other side. They are not going towards Junik. They're going this way, back to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, would you find a suitable place to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think I can fit in one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you did not see any homes set on fire in those villages by the police with your own eyes, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K90 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the first houses that were there, that they were on fire. There was nobody else who could have set them on fire but the police. So after that, a few days later, I went there and I saw that the houses had burned down. The houses by the river. As for the people, I went -- there had been burned by some people who had come. That's what I saw; whereas, these houses - how should I put this? - that the police entered were set on fire probably by the policemen. There was no one else to set fire to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So, again, it's pure speculation and an assumption as to who actually set those fires, you don't know that, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That question --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, [indiscernable].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and it's also not consistent with the answer, at least one interpretation of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I'm done for the day, and I'll hopefully finish up in ten minutes tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Hannis, where are we with the exercise of completing the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the last break I had gone up and sat with my co-counsel here and the interpreter, and they were finalising those changes during this session. I hope it's done. I would, I guess, ask some guidance from the Court. Would you like me to hand the witness a copy of that before he leaves the building today or I had proposed perhaps going through it with him on the record tomorrow, just to ask him if those changes we now have made at these paragraphs accurately reflect the changes he wanted to make. I see advantages to both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I think the latter course, Mr. Hannis. So you'll have it prepared for --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can give it to Defence counsel today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, and that will be dealt with when Mr. Ivetic completes what he has to ask. And then if there's further cross-examination resulting from that, obviously, you would concede that that should take place at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. What I propose to do is ERN this document, call it an amended statement, and we'll give it a different exhibit number if and when it becomes necessary to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Witness K90, that completes today's sitting but you will have to come back again I'm afraid tomorrow morning. Hopefully, your evidence will be finished very quickly tomorrow morning, but you need to come back to resume at 9.00. And I remind you of what I said yesterday, no discussion with anyone at all about your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can now leave the courtroom with the usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of January, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic is correct.
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.,
